name: Thurston County, Washington
source: Compiled locally, November 2026. Verify hours and eligibility by phone before travelling.

items.name: Washington 211
items.notes: Master directory. Routes you to emergency rent help, utility assistance and local nonprofits.

items.name: Lewis-Mason-Thurston Area Agency on Aging (LMTAAA)
items.address: 2404 Heritage Ct SW, Suite A, Olympia
items.notes: The local Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC). Serves adults with disabilities as well as older adults. Help navigating long-term care and caregiver support.

items.name: Center for Independence (CFI)
items.notes: Run by people with disabilities. Independent living skills, peer support, advocacy, finding and training attendants.

items.name: DSHS Home and Community Services (HCS) / Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA)
items.notes: Intake assessment for state-funded Medicaid long-term care, in-home caregivers, or developmental disability case management.

items.name: South Sound Parent to Parent (SSP2P)
items.notes: Family and parent peer support when the disability involves a child or young adult.

items.name: Housing Authority of Thurston County (HATC)
items.notes: Section 8 and Project-Based Vouchers. Documented disability gets priority preference on several waitlists. Also handles reasonable accommodation requests.

items.name: Thurston County Coordinated Entry
items.notes: Single intake system for rapid rehousing, emergency shelter and permanent supportive housing. Use this first if housing is an immediate crisis.

items.name: Community Action Council (CAC)
items.notes: LIHEAP energy and heating bill assistance, weatherization, housing stabilisation programs.

items.name: Intercity Transit, fixed routes
items.notes: All regular buses in Olympia, Lacey, Tumwater and Yelm are fare-free and wheelchair accessible.

items.name: Intercity Transit Dial-A-Lift
items.notes: Door-to-door paratransit van service if a disability keeps you off fixed-route buses. Requires an eligibility application.

items.name: Paratransit Services (Medicaid non-emergency medical transport)
items.notes: Free rides, or gas and mileage reimbursement, to covered medical, dental and behavioral health appointments if you have Apple Health. Book at least two business days ahead.

items.name: Village Vans
items.notes: Free rides for job-related travel: interviews, training, getting to work. For low-income riders.

items.name: COPES / Community First Choice (via DSHS)
items.notes: If you qualify financially and medically for Medicaid long-term care, the state pays for an Individual Provider (a friend or family member you choose and hire) or an agency caregiver for bathing, dressing, cooking, cleaning and errands.

items.name: Catholic Community Services (CCS) Home Care
items.notes: State-trained home care aides for personal care, housework and errands. Accepts DSHS Medicaid and private pay.

items.name: Family Caregiver Support Program (via LMTAAA)
items.notes: Respite care, support groups and limited supplemental supplies if a friend or family member is caring for you unpaid.

items.name: Private-pay home care agencies
items.notes: Comfort Keepers (360) 742-3773, Visiting Angels and ResCare HomeCare all operate locally, for out-of-pocket pay or long-term care insurance.

items.name: Medical Equipment Bank (Thurston County Council on Aging)
items.hours: Tue, Thu and Sat, 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM
items.notes: Free donated wheelchairs, walkers, shower chairs, hospital beds and incontinence supplies. First come, first served. Go in person and fill out a short form.

items.name: Skilled home health agencies
items.notes: Providence SoundHomeCare and Hospice (360) 459-8311, MultiCare Home Health, and Assured Home Health. In-home nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy or wound care ordered by a doctor. Covered by Medicare or Medicaid.

items.name: Thurston County Food Bank (TCFB)
items.notes: Olympia pantry: 220 Thurston Ave NE, Mon/Wed/Fri 10:30 AM to 3:00 PM, free meter parking on distribution days. Lacey pantry: 7027 Martin Way E, Tue and Thu 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM, plus 2nd and 4th Wed 5:00 to 6:30 PM. Ask for the Satellite Coordinator about volunteer home delivery if you are homebound. They also stock ready-to-eat no-cook bags and Ensure or Boost if you ask.

items.name: City Gates Ministries
items.notes: Delivers boxes of groceries to your door by arrangement. Usually calls back within 24 hours. Can accommodate dietary restrictions.

items.name: Capital Christian PEACE Center
items.hours: Mon to Wed, 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM
items.notes: Groceries and basic essentials.

items.name: Hidden Creek Community Church
items.notes: Drive-up or walk-up.

items.name: St. Christopher's Community Church
items.hours: 3rd Thursday of the month, 2:00 to 4:00 PM

items.name: Adventist Community Service Center
items.notes: Emergency food and bread.

items.name: Emergency Outreach Food Pantry
items.notes: Drop-in, no application.

items.name: Tenino Food Bank
items.hours: Tue and Thu, 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM
items.notes: No ID or proof of address required. Does Tuesday deliveries for shut-ins. Carries pet food.

items.name: Olympia Union Gospel Mission
items.hours: Mon to Fri at 6:30 AM, 12:00 PM and 5:00 PM, plus weekend meals
items.notes: Three free hot meals a day, open to anyone.

items.name: The Food Source Foundation
items.address: Next to the downtown Olympia transit centre
items.notes: Free ready-to-eat meals. No ID, no questions asked.

items.name: Senior Nutrition Program (Meals on Wheels via South Sound Seniors)
items.notes: Hot and frozen meal delivery for homebound seniors 60 and over, and eligible adults with disabilities depending on program criteria.
